text:
maria: Heads-up — CI perf alert on staging after onboarding checkpoint v2026-03-15a. p50 stable but p99 token gen latency jumped ~35% on our chat benchmark. Rolling deploy started ~1845990000 so likely related to the new model.
ci-bot: [ALERT] perf/regression: staging p99 token-latency +35% vs baseline — run: ci/staging/perf/1845989 — tags: model:onboard,v2026-03-15a
sam: Ugh. Any obvious metric? kv-cache miss rate? kernel switch events?
yuki: Looking at profiler dumps: KV miss rate up from ~2% -> ~22% for the affected processes. Also saw kernel selection flip from fast-int8-opt to generic-fwd at ~seq-len 1-8 boundary. Profiling snippet (trimmed):
```
2026-03-18T11:15:03Z pid=4231 kernel=fast-int8-opt selected=false reason=token-id-mismatch
2026-03-18T11:15:03Z pid=4231 kv_cache.miss_rate=0.218
2026-03-18T11:15:03Z pid=4231 latency.p99=183ms baseline=136ms
```
oliver: Token-id-mismatch? That smells like tokenizer mapping shift during checkpoint onboarding. Did the new checkpoint change the vocab or added merges?
maria: Yes — model team said they exported a trimmed vocab and re-mapped a bunch of rare tokens to new ids to keep quantization consistent. We probably didn't preserve the token-id compatibility table on-serving-side.
sam: That would explain KV thrash. If token ids change, cached KV keys will be wrong for prefixes => cache misses + different sequence patterns forcing kernel heuristics to choose slower codepath.
yuki: Agreed. I ran a quick simulation: remapping a prefix of 8 tokens generates a 12% throughput regression in our microbench due to increased KV misses and smaller batch coalescing.
ci-bot: [CI INFO] perf-regression-check: bisect run queued (#bisect-1845991)
maria: Can someone run the bisect on the model-onboard PR/commit? I want the exact commit that introduced id-shift.
oliver: I'm on it. Running bisect across model-export commits 572..579. Expect ~20 min.
sam: Meanwhile, two mitigation paths: 1) revert the staging deploy (stop rollout) and roll back to previous checkpoint; 2) implement compatibility mapping layer on the tokenizer to translate new ids back to old ids for cached prefixes.
maria: Revert is fastest. We should block production rollout until we confirm.
deploy-bot: rollback started for service=rl-inference-staging, rollout_id=stg-2026-03-18-11:30 — status: in_progress
yuki: If we do compatibility mapping, it's not just a small table — need to ensure mapping is deterministic across tokenization modes (BPE vs sentencepiece). Might be messy for on-prem customers too.
oliver: Bisect result: commit 576 is culprit — exporter script changed token ordering to prioritize subword merges which shifted ids. Repro is 100%.
maria: OK. Revert staging immediately and open a hotfix to keep id ordering stable in the exporter. Sam, can you draft the tokenizer compatibility shim as fallback if we ever accept id-reordering in future?
sam: Yep. Plan: (A) short-term: revert deploy (already in progress), add an automated check in runtime CI that computes token-id diff between model metadata and last-served-vocab and fails rollout if > 5% shift. (B) medium-term: compatibility shim + KV cache namespace versioning so old cache entries are invalidated safely.
yuki: Also tweak kernel selection heuristic to consider kv_cache.miss_rate: if miss_rate spikes >10% during warmup, prefer robust kernel (fast-generic) with better handling of short-seq churn until steady state.
maria: Good call. That avoids immediate latency cliffs during onboarding. Add as quick config flag we can toggle per-deploy.
deploy-bot: rollback succeeded for service=rl-inference-staging — rollout complete, version=v2026-03-14b restored
ci-bot: [CI NOTE] bisect complete — culprit commit: exporter#576 — author: @model-team — tagging @model-team for follow-up
oliver: I'll open PR to revert exporter change + add unit test to prevent id reordering. PR link: https://git.internal/redwood/model-exporter/pull/597
sam: I'll add the runtime CI check (token-id-diff threshold) and a quick perf test to catch KV thrash in presubmit.
maria: I'll block the main rollout until model-team confirms corrected exporter and we pass the token-id diff check in staging.
ci-bot: [ACTION] Created ticket PERF-8632: onboarding token-id drift -> KV thrash -> kernel misroute. Assigned: sam, priority=P0.
oliver: model-team pinged. They're preparing a rebuild with preserved id ordering. ETA ~3 hours.
yuki: After fix: we'll run canary with `--kernel-fallback-on-kv-spike` flag enabled for extra safety.
maria: Sounds good. Thanks everyone. Keep updates in this thread. :thumbsup:
